title-group.article-title: Fluid Resuscitation Protocols in Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Multicenter Comparative Analysis

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) represents an acute life-threatening emergency characterized by hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and ketonemia.

sec.title: Study Design and Patient Population
sec.p: We conducted a retrospective cohort study across four tertiary academic intensive care units examining balanced crystalloids versus 0.9% normal saline.

sec.title: Electrolyte Monitoring Protocol
sec.p: Serum potassium was evaluated every two hours. Intravenous insulin infusion was held if serum potassium was below 3.3 mEq/L.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Time to resolution of acidosis was significantly shorter in the balanced crystalloid group compared to normal saline (median 13.0 vs 16.5 hours; p = 0.004).

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Resuscitation with balanced crystalloids mitigates hyperchloremic non-anion gap metabolic acidosis and hastens DKA resolution.
